title: Cellular Jail - The Symbol of India’s Freedom Struggle in Andaman
content:
Cellular Jail, 

Located in Port Blair in the beautiful Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Cellular Jail is one of the most significant historical monuments in India. Popularly known as Kala Pani, this colonial prison stands as a powerful reminder of the sacrifices made by Indian freedom fighters during the British rule.

Today, Cellular Jail is not just a tourist attraction but also an emotional destination that tells the stories of courage, pain, and patriotism. Thousands of travelers visit this iconic place every year to experience its history, architecture, and the inspiring Light & Sound Show.

Whether you are a history lover, a traveler exploring Andaman, or someone interested in India’s independence movement, a visit to Cellular Jail is truly unforgettable.

History of Cellular Jail

The history of Cellular Jail dates back to the late 19th century during British colonial rule. After the Revolt of 1857, the British government wanted a remote location to imprison Indian freedom fighters and political prisoners. The Andaman Islands, surrounded by the sea and isolated from mainland India, became the perfect location.

Construction of Cellular Jail began in 1896 and was completed in 1906. The prison was specifically designed to isolate prisoners completely from each other so that they could not communicate or organize revolts.

Many famous Indian freedom fighters were imprisoned here, including:

  • Veer Savarkar
  • Batukeshwar Dutt
  • Yogendra Shukla
  • Ullaskar Dutta
  • Barindra Kumar Ghosh

Prisoners were subjected to extremely harsh punishments, forced labor, solitary confinement, and inhuman treatment. The jail became a symbol of British oppression and Indian resistance.

Cellular Jail has been converted into a National Memorial to honor the sacrifices of India’s freedom fighters.

Why is Cellular Jail Called Kala Pani?

The term Kala Pani means “Black Water.” During British rule, prisoners sent to the Andaman Islands were considered completely cut off from society and family because crossing the sea was viewed as social exile.

The punishment of being sent to Cellular Jail was considered one of the harshest penalties during colonial times. Prisoners suffered physical torture, emotional trauma, and complete isolation.

Because of this painful history, Cellular Jail became widely known as Kala Pani.

Architecture of Cellular Jail

Cellular Jail is an architectural masterpiece built with a unique design.

Key Features:

  • The jail originally had 7 wings
  • The structure was built in a radial pattern from a central tower
  • It contained around 693 solitary cells
  • Each cell measured approximately 13.5 ft × 7 ft
  • Cells were designed in a way that prisoners could not communicate with each other
  • There were no dormitories, only isolated cells

The central tower allowed guards to monitor all seven wings at once.

Unfortunately, only three wings remain today as the others were demolished after independence.

Major Attractions Inside Cellular Jail

1. Prison Cells

The solitary confinement cells are the most emotional part of the jail. Visitors can witness the tiny rooms where freedom fighters spent years under difficult conditions.

The cell of Veer Savarkar is one of the major highlights and attracts visitors from across the country.

2. Light and Sound Show

The Light & Sound Show at Cellular Jail is one of the most popular attractions in Port Blair.

The show beautifully narrates the history of the jail, the struggles of freedom fighters, and the brutal treatment during British rule. The storytelling, lighting effects, and patriotic atmosphere create a deeply emotional experience.

The show is usually available in both Hindi and English.

3. Museum and Galleries

The jail complex also includes museums and galleries displaying:

  • Photographs of freedom fighters
  • Historical documents
  • Prison records
  • Paintings and artifacts
  • Information about the Indian freedom movement

4. Martyrs’ Memorial

The memorial honors the brave freedom fighters who sacrificed their lives for India’s independence.

5. Watch Tower

Visitors can climb the central watch tower to enjoy panoramic views of Port Blair and understand the prison’s radial design.

Best Time to Visit Cellular Jail

The best time to visit Cellular Jail is between October and May when the weather in Andaman is pleasant and suitable for sightseeing.

Weather Guide:

  • October to February: Cool and comfortable
  • March to May: Warm but good for tourism
  • June to September: Monsoon season with heavy rainfall

Evening visits are highly recommended if you want to attend the Light & Sound Show.

 

Cellular Jail Timings

Opening Hours:

  • Morning: 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM
  • Afternoon: 1:30 PM to 5:00 PM

The jail remains closed on Mondays and national holidays.

Light & Sound Show timings may vary depending on the season.

Entry Fee for Cellular Jail

Approximate charges may include:

  • Entry Ticket for Indian Nationals
  • Separate charges for Foreign Nationals
  • Additional ticket for Light & Sound Show
  • Camera or video recording charges (if applicable)

Visitors are advised to check the latest ticket prices before visiting.

How to Reach Cellular Jail

By Air: The nearest airport is Veer Savarkar International Airport in Port Blair. Regular flights are available from major Indian cities like:

Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bangalore, Hyderabad - From the airport, Cellular Jail is located approximately 4 km away.

By Road: Cellular Jail is well connected by local taxis, auto-rickshaws, and private vehicles within Port Blair.

Things to Know Before Visiting

  • Carry a valid ID proof
  • Wear comfortable clothes and footwear
  • Photography may be restricted in certain areas
  • Reach early during peak tourist season
  • Attend the Light & Sound Show for the complete experience
  • Maintain silence and respect the historical importance of the site

Emotional Significance of Cellular Jail

Cellular Jail is not just a building made of bricks and iron. It represents the suffering, sacrifice, and determination of India’s freedom fighters.

Walking through the prison corridors gives visitors a deep emotional connection to India’s independence struggle. The stories of bravery inspire patriotism and respect for those who fought for the nation.

Many travelers describe their visit to Cellular Jail as emotional, educational, and unforgettable.

Travel Tips for Visitors

  • Visit during evening hours for cooler weather
  • Book Light & Sound Show tickets in advance during peak season
  • Spend at least 2-3 hours exploring the complex
  • Read the historical displays carefully for a better understanding
  • Combine your visit with Ross Island and North Bay tour
